headline: 54 killed, 6 lakh affected as floods and landslides hit 7 districts
summary: Severe flooding and landslides across seven districts have left over 600,000 people affected, with the death toll rising to 54.
details: Floods and landslides across seven districts in Bangladesh have resulted in 54 deaths and affected more than 600,000 people.
The disaster has caused widespread devastation, with Prothom Alo reporting the death toll had reached 51 before further updates increased it to 54.
In the northeast, rivers have surged above danger levels, contributing to the severe flooding in the region.
Additionally, five people were killed by lightning strikes amid the volatile weather conditions.
The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has warned that heavy rain is expected to continue across the country for the next five days.
Emergency responses are ongoing as thousands of homes and crops remain submerged under water.
caption:

headline: Cost of model mosques rose from Tk 13cr to 21cr: Govt to probe corruption
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed calls the cost escalation in model mosque projects under the previous government 'disgraceful' and orders a mosque-by-mosque investigation.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has announced that the government will conduct mosque-by-mosque investigations into the construction of model mosques under the ousted Awami League government.
The probe focuses on how the cost of constructing a single model mosque rose from Tk 13 crore to Tk 21 crore, a jump the Home Minister described as 'disgraceful' corruption in the name of Islam.
During a parliamentary session, MP Zainul Abdin Farroque highlighted that the model mosque in Senbagh is in disrepair, with water leaking through the structure and poor accessibility.
Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal also raised concerns about the the model mosque in Durgapur, noting it is nearly inaccessible and has been nicknamed the 'Taj Mahal of Durgapur' by locals.
Salahuddin Ahmed stated that projects were designed to loot money, with estimates being multiplied and implementation periods extended from five to seven years to facilitate corruption.
The Home Minister referenced a white paper by economist Debapriya Bhattacharya, noting that mega budgets were often adopted for mega projects to enable 'mega corruption'.
In a separate update, the Religious Affairs Minister informed Parliament that out of 537,550.98 acres of registered waqf property, 27.53 acres have been recovered from illegal occupation.
caption:
Costs jumped from Tk 13 crore to Tk 21 crore per mosque. The government is now probing 'disgraceful' corruption in model mosque projects.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has announced that the government will conduct mosque-by-mosque investigations into the construction of model mosques under the ousted Awami League government.

The probe focuses on how the cost of constructing a single model mosque rose from Tk 13 crore to Tk 21 crore, a jump the Home Minister described as 'disgraceful' corruption in the name of Islam.

During a parliamentary session, MP Zainul Abdin Farroque highlighted that the model mosque in Senbagh is in disrepair, with water leaking through the structure and poor accessibility.

Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal also raised concerns about the the model mosque in Durgapur, noting it is nearly inaccessible and has been nicknamed the 'Taj Mahal of Durgapur' by locals.

Salahuddin Ahmed stated that projects were designed to loot money, with estimates being multiplied and implementation periods extended from five to seven years to facilitate corruption.

The Home Minister referenced a white paper by economist Debapriya Bhattacharya, noting that mega budgets were often adopted for mega projects to enable 'mega corruption'.

In a separate update, the Religious Affairs Minister informed Parliament that out of 537,550.98 acres of registered waqf property, 27.53 acres have been recovered from illegal occupation.
